name: Extended Side Angle
hero_alt: Extended Side Angle, seen from the side
meta_description: Front knee short of 90°, back knee bending, back heel lifting, top arm drifting? Four things usually hold back Extended Side Angle, and a daily exercise for each.
og_description: Four things usually hold back Extended Side Angle, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
lede: Front knee over the ankle at a right angle, one long line from your back heel to your top fingertips. Here’s the rubric Posewise measures it against, and what to train when you miss.
rubric_intro: Posewise checks six things from the side. Here’s what good looks like.

rubric.name: Front knee
rubric.good: Bent to a right angle, over the ankle

rubric.name: Torso
rubric.good: Long over your front thigh, not sinking onto it

rubric.name: Top arm
rubric.good: Reaching past your ear, in line with your side body

rubric.name: Chest
rubric.good: Turned open, not facing the floor

fixes.outcome: your front knee will reach a 90° bend.
fixes.why: The shape is there, the depth isn’t. That usually points to leg strength, not technique.
fixes.cue: Bend your front knee to 90°, knee over ankle.

fixes.action: Lengthen your inner thighs and quads
fixes.why: Tight groin and quad muscles pull the back knee into a bend.
fixes.cue: Press through your back foot and straighten the leg.

fixes.outcome: your back heel will stay planted.
fixes.why: Tight calves cap how far the back ankle bends, so the heel peels up and the long line breaks.
fixes.cue: Press the outer edge of your back foot down.

fixes.outcome: your top arm will extend in one line past your ear.
fixes.why: When shoulder range runs out, the top arm drifts forward or stops short instead of reaching overhead.
fixes.cue: Reach your top arm long past your ear.

cues: And two cues: keep your side body long over your front thigh instead of sinking onto it, and roll your top shoulder back to open your chest.

faq.q: Should my hand touch the floor in Extended Side Angle?
faq.a: Only if your torso stays long. Rest your forearm on your front thigh or your hand on a block instead of collapsing to reach the floor.

faq.q: Where should my front knee be in Extended Side Angle?
faq.a: Stacked over your ankle at about 90°, pointing toward your middle toes. If it drifts past your toes, widen your stance.

faq.q: Why does my back foot lift in Extended Side Angle?
faq.a: Usually tight calves or a stance that’s too long. Turn your back toes in slightly and press the outer edge of the foot down.

faq.q: Where should I look in Extended Side Angle?
faq.a: Up toward your top hand if your neck is comfortable, otherwise straight ahead or down at the floor.

faq.q: How can I check my Extended Side Angle form at home?
faq.a: Film yourself from the side. Or use Posewise, an iPhone app that measures your Extended Side Angle with the camera, speaks corrections as you hold it, and builds a six-minute daily plan for what it finds.

llms_summary: the four things that usually hold back Extended Side Angle (leg strength for a 90° front knee, tight groin and quads bending the back leg, tight calves lifting the back heel, stiff shoulders breaking the top-arm line), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
